title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. M is a free Z/4Z-module of rank 2; in the source this is the 4-torsion E[4] of an elliptic curve, in characteristic not 2. This page closes a bracketed digression that began on the previous page. That digression asked what extra data must be added to the unoriented octahedron Delta_M = M*/{±1} in order to recover M. Equivalently: how does the extension 1 -> {±1} -> Gl(M) -> Gl(M)' ≅ Aut_oct(Delta) -> 1 lift torsors?

(1) Recalled diagram (23). The group I read as Gl_Lambda(M) = GL(M), with Lambda = Z/4, maps to two groups:
- the symmetric group S_I of a 4-element set I, through the affine group AGL(M_0) ≅ S_4, where M_0 = M/2M;
- the dihedral group D_Q of a combinatorial square Q.
Both map to {±1}: S_I by the signature, D_Q by the character chi_c, which records the action on the two 'codiagonals' (pairs of opposite edges) of Q. The square is cartesian, so
GL(2,Z/4) ≅ S_4 ×_{C_2} D_4.
Order check: 24·8/2 = 96 = |GL(2,Z/4)|. The kernel of the composite map to S_3 = GL(M_0) is V_4 × ker(chi_c) = V_4 × V_4 ≅ F_2^4 = 1 + 2End(M_0), which is consistent.

(2) Stacky reformulation. Because the square of groups is a fibre product over surjections, BGL(2,Z/4) is the 2-fibre product BS_4 ×_{BC_2} BD_4. Concretely, giving M is equivalent to giving a triple (I, Q, K):
- I is a 4-element set;
- Q is a combinatorial square;
- K is an isomorphism from the 2-element set C_Q of codiagonals of Q to the orientation torsor omega_I of I (orderings of I modulo even permutations).

(3) Translation in terms of Q. The face-colour set C_Delta of the octahedron (its 8 faces carry a 2-colouring) is identified with F(Delta)/M_0, then with P_{M}/F_2 = S_Q/F_2, then with D_Q, the set of diagonals of Q.

(4) Consequence for the octahedron. Giving Delta (instead of M) amounts to giving I together with the two 2-element sets C (≅ omega_I, the codiagonals) and D (the diagonals). The pair (C,D) is a torsor under D_4/Z(D_4) ≅ F_2 × F_2 (equally D_4^ab).
- This matches Aut(octahedron) = S_4 ×_{C_2} V_4 ≅ S_4 × C_2, of order 48.
- Recovering M therefore means lifting this V_4-torsor to a D_4-torsor, i.e. finding a square Q whose diagonal and codiagonal sets are the given D and C.
- The kernel {±1} of GL -> GL/±1 corresponds to the centre of D_4 (rotation by 180°).

The page breaks off there ('...'). The next page ('Récapitulation partielle') supplies the canonical construction Q_M = P_M/M_0 and the bijections C_Q ≅ omega, D_Q ≅ face colours, or(Q) ≅ det(M)* = mu.

Purpose. This is a combinatorial-geometric model of full level-4 structures (octahedron = P^1(Z/4), the 6 cusps of X(4)), for the moduli of elliptic curves in characteristic ≠ 2.
errors: Notation drift: C_Delta (face colours) is identified with D_Q (diagonals), while the text then calls the two 2-element sets 'C (≅ omega_I) and D corresponding to diagonals and codiagonals'. The order is reversed relative to the assignment C = codiagonals, D = diagonals used on the next page. This is cosmetic.

The top node F_2^omega ≅ V(S_Q), with its arrows into the diagram, is not coherent as drawn. The kernel of GL(M) -> S_I is ker(chi_c) ≅ V_4, not an F_2 of order 2. The decoration presumably refers to the central extension or to a different piece of diagram (23). It is unclear from the page alone.
The page ends mid-thought ('...'): the lifting of the (C,D) torsor to a square Q is posed but not carried out here (it is done on the next page).

ideas.what: Isomorphism GL(2,Z/4) ≅ S_4 ×_{C_2} D_4 (fibre product over sign and a dihedral character), via GL(2,Z/4) -> AGL(2,F_2) ≅ S_4
ideas.modern_name: structure of GL_2(Z/4Z) as a subdirect product
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore finite group theory; appears implicitly in work on 4-adic/mod-4 Galois images of elliptic curves (e.g. Rouse–Zureick-Brown) – no specific attribution known

ideas.what: Equivalence of groupoids: free rank-2 Z/4-modules <-> triples (4-set I, combinatorial square Q, iso codiagonals(Q) ≅ orientations(I)), i.e. BGL_2(Z/4) ≃ BS_4 ×_{BC_2} BD_4
ideas.modern_name: torsor/groupoid description of level-4 structures; 2-fibre product of classifying stacks
ideas.usually_credited_to: not specifically credited; standard torsor reasoning

ideas.what: Octahedron Delta_M = M*/±1 = P^1(Z/4) with Aut ≅ S_4 × C_2; recovering M from Delta = lifting a V_4 = D_4/Z-torsor to a D_4-torsor (a square with prescribed diagonals/codiagonals)
ideas.modern_name: octahedral geometry of X(4)/level-4 structure; obstruction to lifting along central extension 1->C_2->D_4->V_4->1
ideas.usually_credited_to: octahedral symmetry of X(4): Klein; the lifting formulation unattributed

missed.claim: An explicit, intrinsic combinatorial model of a full level-4 structure: E[4] is described by a 4-set, a square, and a matching between codiagonals and the orientation torsor of the 4-set. The octahedron Delta = P^1(E[4]) captures exactly the part modulo ±1. This is an elegant reformulation, not a new theorem, and is unlikely to surprise specialists.
missed.quote: la donnée de M équivalant à celle des triples (I, Q, K), où I est un ens. à quatre éléments, Q un carré combinatoire, et K un isom K : C_Q ≃ ω_I
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Could give a clean, choice-free description of the stack of level-4 structures (X(4) and its cusps) useful in explicit moduli/Galois-image computations, but the group theory is routine.

deep.surprise_reason: Correct and neat but routine finite-group/torsor bookkeeping (GL_2(Z/4) as S_4 ×_{C_2} D_4, octahedral model of P^1(Z/4)). It is part of a private working-out of level-4 structures, with no evident unpublished theorem or missed connection.
transcription_corrections: Opening line is likely 'Je me rapporte au diagramme (23)' (or 'J'en reviens au diagramme (23)'), with F_2^omega being a node of the diagram, not part of the sentence.
'En donnant de Q, on a' should read 'En termes de Q, on a'.
'ens des diagonales de Q — dans la donnée de l'octaèdre Δ en lieu de M' should read 'ens. des diagonales de Q — donc la donnée de l'octaèdre Δ au lieu de M ↔ (I,Q,K)'.
'sur D_4 B(D_4) ≃ F_2×F_2' is probably 'sous D_4/Z(D_4)' or 'D_4^{ab} ≃ F_2 × F_2' (both are V_4), with 'D_4' written after a crossed-out attempt.
'qui est fait donc valoir en un torseur sous D_4' should read 'qu'il faut donc relever en un torseur sous D_4'.
'En encore' should read 'Ou encore' / 'En d'autres termes'; 'donc on a déjà' should read 'dont on a déjà'.
